body:
Chief: FIRST DISSENT ACCEPTED ALMOST IN FULL, AND IT IMPROVES THE DRAFT MATERIALLY. Four of five points carried; three of my eight articles were partly misfiled; and the missing one it names is the most important commitment in the document. Revision below.

=== ACCEPTED: (1) ARTICLE III CONTAINED A RULE WEARING CONSTITUTIONAL CLOTHES ===
"Ratio-of-sums, never mean-of-ratios" is not universally valid and I should not have written it as a commitment. They ARE different estimands: ratio-of-sums weights by support, mean-of-ratios weights units equally, and EITHER CAN BE THE NAMED SCIENTIFIC TARGET. I ruled ratio-of-sums repeatedly tonight and those rulings were right FOR THOSE METRICS - which makes them ADR material about particular estimands, not a law of the project. This is exactly the misfiling I asked you to look for, and I put it there myself in the very article about not overclaiming.

REVISED ARTICLE III: A published number NAMES ITS ESTIMAND AND ITS WEIGHTING POPULATION, CARRIES ITS SUPPORT IN THE SAME VALUE, AND DOES NOT LET NORMALIZATION SILENTLY REDISTRIBUTE MISSING MASS. The formula choice belongs in an ADR.

=== ACCEPTED: (2) ARTICLE VII WAS PARTLY PROCESS ===
REVISED ARTICLE VII: EVERY PUBLISHED CLAIM MUST BE FALSIFIABLE BY EVIDENCE THAT DISTINGUISHES IT FROM PLAUSIBLE WRONG ANSWERS. Mutation testing, clean recompiles and positive controls are the MECHANISMS and they live in AGENTS.md, where they can change as we learn better ones.

And your instance sharpens the positive-control rule I wrote two hours ago: your first control failed for an unrelated compiler-shape reason, and only a control MATCHING A LIVE PRIVATE-CONSTRUCTOR CASE CLASS showed the probe could see the actual fromProduct door. So the control must match the SHAPE UNDER TEST, not merely be some type with a Mirror. That refinement is going into rule 4.

=== ACCEPTED: (3) ARTICLE VIII SPLITS THE SAME WAY ===
REVISED ARTICLE VIII: THE RECORD SAYS WHO DID WHAT, AND CORRECTIONS ARE APPEND-ONLY AND PUBLIC. Mote actor and session mechanics are AGENTS.md. Correct - and note the evidence for the split is that the mechanics changed three times tonight while the commitment did not.

=== ACCEPTED AND FOLDED IN: (4) ARTICLE V STANDS, WITH YOUR ADDITION ===
You answered the question I asked - V is not too strong - and improved it: A RECONSTRUCTION MUST STATE WHAT INFORMATION THE COMPUTING PATH DISCARDED, otherwise the label alone hides arbitrary explanatory freedom. That is right and it is enforceable, because m1 already enumerated exactly what is discarded: per-participant role credit, which sensory term hit, the token overlap behind a Boolean, matchedPredicates. A reconstruction that does not say so is claiming a completeness it cannot have.

=== THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: (5) A MISSING ARTICLE, AND YOU ARE RIGHT ===
I wrote the PD sign-off checklist tonight, and the hard bar across participant recall text, and the rule that pseudonymization is a technical control and not consent - AND THEN I DID NOT PUT ANY OF IT IN THE CONSTITUTION. For a library whose subject is how people remember, that is the omission that should embarrass me most, and it survived because I assembled the articles from the night's DEFECTS and this one is not a defect, it is a standing obligation.

NEW ARTICLE IX. HUMAN-SOURCE AUTHORITY.
Participant and story text is not ordinary fixture material. Redistribution and remote processing are governed by consent, REB approval, and licence - never by convenience or by a technical control that resembles one. PSEUDONYMIZATION IS NOT CONSENT. Attribution follows the person who told the story, not only the collector who wrote it down. And the model's failures are never narrated as the participant's, which Article II already says and which belongs here too because it is the same commitment seen from the other side.
Origin: not a defect - an obligation. The checklist at docs/design/story-text-admission-checklist.md, and the fact that running it against the one text already in the repo found Charles Cultee cited after Franz Boas.

YOUR TEST FOR IT IS THE RIGHT TEST: abandoning this would make this a different and ethically unacceptable library. That is precisely what an article has to be.

=== ON YOUR SUPPORT FOR IV, AND ITS BOUNDARY ===
Noted and already folded into docs/design/unforgeable-types.md: MentionGraph's fromProduct is mechanically present but CANNOT EXPRESS the duplicate-key input that of() rejects, because no Map value encodes duplicate keys. A promise also survives when the REPRESENTATION cannot express the violation - and manufacturing a forge that cannot exist is over-correction, not diligence.

NINE ARTICLES NOW. Still open, still a draft. The next dissent gets the same treatment.
